questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic opportunity was crucial for my decision. Being able to study at two prestigious universities in the field of international law at Geneva Graduate Institute and University of Geneva through the highly motivated and demanding Certificate of Transnational Law (CTL) has indeed given me a special insight of international law.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival to Geneva, I received all the necessary administrative and academic information needed for my stay. During the first orientation week, both the IT department and the respective faculties had organized an orientation programme.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: See the above mentioned comment.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The exchange agreement between UCPH and University of Geneva allowed me to directly apply for accommodation through the residences owned by the university and also to the Cité L'universitaire de Geneve, which is a large common student residence.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: See the above mentioned comment.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration process consists of a two folded process. The first process starts two weeks after the beginning of the semester, where you have to sign op for the courses that you want to follow. The second step is similar, since you have to register for the exams in the afore mentioned courses that you have decided to sign up for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always receive additional help either through your exchange coordinator, your faculty or through the general office for incoming exchange students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for all the classes I wanted to attend.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is important to carefully read the received emails regarding the registration process, since it contains some important deadlines that you need to respect.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All my courses were at the master level at the faculty of law, since all courses at the bachelor level were all teached in french.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching of style varied a lot. Some of the courses including a requirement for active participation while some courses did not even required physical presence.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- European competition law (6 ECTS), 
- Comparative law: contract law (6 ECTS)
- International Humanitarian Law (6 ECTS)
- Compliance with international law (6 ECTS)
- Business and human rights: politics, law and policy (6 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend law students to apply for the Certificate in Transnational Law, which allows you to apply for two courses at the Graduate Institute.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not expect such a high cost for daily shopping, especially groceries and general living expenses.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The general costs of living is higher than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: During the first orientation week, you will be presented to all the possible clubs and societies that you can become a member of during the semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend signing up for a sport or gym.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Due to the central location of Geneva, I would recommend to visit France and Italy during your stay.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Geneva is one of the most international cities in the world with a very high percentage of international citizens living there so it is very easy to live there.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Some of the locals do not speak English fluently and it can, therefore, be difficult to hold a conversation with them, as a large part of them primarily speak French or German.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The culture of Geneva is very international but on the other hand, it is also a very conservative town as regarding the night life and the fact that all supermarkets and shops are closed every Sunday.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: First, you have to get an accommodation through the university agreement, since it is too expensive to rent an apartment or studio on the private market. Secondly, you should expect to put some effort and hours into your studies. Thirdly, you should participate and sign up for some of the clubs and societies that are being offered by the university in order to fully experience the exchange life as well as meeting new people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is important to socialize a lot in the beginning in order to find some new friends during your exchange.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange was definitely to study together with so many international students from all over the world and hear there different perspectives on law and life in general.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during my stay was to speak and improve my french.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
